title: Delta Air Lines Won't Get Its Boeing 787-10s Until 2031, So The Airbus A350-1000 Has To ...
description:
Delta Air Lines is constructing a premium-heavy flagship operation centered around Seoul Incheon International Airport(ICN) and its foundational joint venture with Korean Air.
The newly ordered Boeing 787-10 fleet will not arrive until 2031, and so, the Airbus A350-1000 must carry that complex commercial strategy entirely on its own for years until the orders begin to arrive.
To support these high-frequency transpacific rotations, Delta is banking on sophisticated interior engineering capable of sustaining passenger comfort across ultra-long-haul durations.
To capture maximum revenue on transpacific routes, Delta designed its A350-1000 cabin around an unprecedented premium density.
Delta Air Lines' strategic reliance on the A350-1000 to spearhead its transpacific expansion highlights the high-stakes reality of modern fleet planning.
text:
Delta Air Lines is constructing a premium-heavy flagship operation centered around Seoul Incheon International Airport(ICN) and its foundational joint venture with Korean Air. The newly ordered Boeing 787-10 fleet will not arrive until 2031, and so, the Airbus A350-1000 must carry that complex commercial strategy entirely on its own for years until the orders begin to arrive.

How does placing the immediate transpacific burden on 20 A350-1000 airframes, scheduled to debut in early 2027, shape Delta's long-term competitive posture against rival US legacies? What forces compelled the airline to commit to a massive widebody modernization wave while accepting a multi-year delivery gap for its Dreamliner order? This article will cover exactly that.

Delta's New Asian Base

Delta is confirmed to debut its flagship Airbus A350-1000 aircraft in early 2027, deploying the widebody airframes on high-demand routes connecting Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL) to ICN, along with Detroit Metropolitan Wayne County Airport (DTW) to ICN, as detailed in reports from View Times. The deployment formalizes a major shift for the airline, leveraging Delta's joint venture with Korean Air to cement ICN as its main Asian transit hub. By funneling connecting traffic through ICN rather than traditional Tokyo gateways, Delta gains more efficient access to secondary markets across East Asia and Southeast Asia than it had before.

The Korean Air joint venture functions as an integrated commercial engine, aligning schedules, pricing, and frequent flyer benefits to capture high-yield corporate traffic moving between North America and Asian financial centers. According to Delta operational filings, passengers arriving at ICN on Delta flights can seamlessly connect to Korean Air's extensive regional network, bypassing the friction of multi-carrier itineraries. This partnership is incredibly important to Delta's transpacific profitability, because with it, every widebody flight departing US mega-hubs is backed by robust feed from both sides of the Pacific.

To support these high-frequency transpacific rotations, Delta is banking on sophisticated interior engineering capable of sustaining passenger comfort across ultra-long-haul durations. As Delta introduces the A350-1000, the layout of the cabin directly influences passenger acquisition and retention among high-paying business travelers who regularly compare legacy carriers with joint venture alternatives.

A Truly Premium Cabin Offering?

To capture maximum revenue on transpacific routes, Delta designed its A350-1000 cabin around an unprecedented premium density. As outlined in industry reports from Aviation Outlook, the aircraft features 53 Delta One Suites and 48 Premium Select seats, dedicating over 40% of total floor space to premium passengers. This heavy premium concentration reflects management's bet that corporate travel demand across the Pacific will continue to prioritize upgraded space and privacy over sheer economy volume.

Inside the cabin, the A350-1000 introduces Delta's next-generation Delta One Suite, which features fully flat beds measuring 6.5 feet (1.98 meters) long and personal entertainment screens using 24-inch 4K QLED technology. Furthermore, Airbus announcements confirm that Delta's 20 A350-1000s will be equipped with a first-of-its-kind multi-orbit inflight connectivity solution. With Hughes low-earth-orbit and geosynchronous-earth-orbit technology integrated through Airbus HBCplus, passengers will experience uninterrupted high-speed internet connectivity throughout transoceanic flights.

Integrating these advanced hardware amenities aligns directly with Delta's broader widebody modernization strategy. By outfitting its flagship fleet with next-generation suites and high-speed multi-orbit connectivity, the carrier can offer a standardized luxury product that reinforces its competitive edge in both corporate and premium leisure markets.

The Start Of The Modernization

Delta kicked off a massive widebody modernization campaign in the first half of 2026, placing firm orders for 95 new aircraft to replace aging twinjets across its international network. As detailed by Airways Magazine, this record order spree follows a phenomenal financial year in 2025, during which the carrier generated $5 billion in pre-tax profit on $63.4 billion in operating revenue. The order book includes 30 firm 787-10s alongside 30 options: 16 A330-900neos, 15 A350-900s, and 34 A321neos.

The multi-type acquisition drives a clear fleet segmentation strategy across Delta's global network. Network planners intend to deploy the newly ordered A350-1000s and A350-900s on ultra-long-haul transpacific sectors and high-demand Middle Eastern corridors, such as routes to Riyadh Airport(RUH), though the debut of this specific route has been delayed amid regional safety concerns. The incoming A330-900neos will primarily serve transatlantic markets and South American routes. This division ensures that each aircraft variant operates within its optimal range and payload envelope, maximizing fuel efficiency and reducing unit operating costs across distinct geographical regions.

The A350-900s and A330neos ultimately handle core international growth in the near term, but the delayed arrival of the 787-10 fleet shifts the real heavy lifting onto the A350-1000 program, turning it into the central pillar of Delta's long-haul evolution, a role that was not necessarily envisaged when the -1000 variant entered Delta's fleet plans.

Is The A350-1000 Enough In The Meantime?

The scheduled arrival of Delta's 30 firm 787-10s beginning in 2031 has created a significant operational timeline gap. Industry reports from Simple Flying show that manufacturing backlogs and production slot allocations pushed the first Dreamliner deliveries five years out from the initial order announcement. Consequently, Delta will need to rely entirely on its Airbus widebody deliveries to bridge the gap between retiring older 767s and 777s and the eventual arrival of the 787-10 fleet.

From an operating economics standpoint, the A350-1000 brings immediate relief through advanced propulsion technology. Powered by Rolls-Royce Trent XWB-97 engines, the A350-1000 delivers up to 20% lower fuel burn per seat-mile compared to the older aircraft it replaces, supported by Airbus data indicating a 15% to 25% lower overall seat-mile cost than legacy widebody competitors. However, concentrating all ultra-long-haul growth onto a single Airbus flagship type exposes Delta to supply chain vulnerabilities, spare-engine availability constraints, and intensive maintenance scheduling pressures across its Atlanta maintenance bases.

Keeping these manufacturing delays under control is a great challenge for Delta and demands rigorous maintenance planning and careful route allocation. Network managers have to extract maximum utilization from initial A350-1000 deliveries, and at the same time, safeguard spare parts inventory and pilot training pipelines to prevent any potential disruptions from becoming more problematic across the broader transpacific network.

Still A Wait To Be At Full Strength

Relying on a constrained initial batch of airframes isn't ideal from a network scheduling standpoint. Although Delta holds 20 firm A350-1000 orders, contractually committed delivery schedules allocate only the first eight aircraft to arrive through 2027, following earlier projections that anticipated 2026 handovers, as per Engine Cowl. The limited initial inventory means network planners will need to concentrate the new flagships strictly on core profit generators like the ATL and DTW routes to ICN, leaving little spare capacity for speculative route launches.

Expanding into emerging long-haul markets, such as launching service to RUH or evaluating a potential return to Indian airspace, depends entirely on subsequent A350-1000 deliveries arriving in 2028 and beyond and how fast those actually come in. If delivery slots slip or global supply chain snags delay airframe handovers, Delta will have little choice but to defer secondary route expansion plans to protect frequencies on its crucial Korean Air joint-venture corridors. Balancing high-yielding joint venture commitments with adventurous new city pairs will really show the elasticity of Delta's rather narrow widebody inventory.

Balancing these competing operational pressures dictates the pace of Delta's international network evolution. Because the initial wave of A350-1000 deliveries will have to cover essential joint-venture routes to ICN, any unexpected supply chain friction or maintenance issue directly impacts the airline's capacity to test new long-haul markets and, therefore, compete more fiercely with its Transpacific rivals.

Is Help Needed?

Delta Air Lines' strategic reliance on the A350-1000 to spearhead its transpacific expansion highlights the high-stakes reality of modern fleet planning. Delta has set its operational focus around Seoul Incheon and the Korean Air joint venture while accepting a five-year wait for its Boeing 787-10 deliveries. As a result, the carrier is placing an immense operational bet on a single Airbus flagship arriving in stages. What this shows is that network success depends as much on delivery schedule timing as on onboard product innovation.

Sustaining this ambitious strategy through 2031 will be hard, requiring flawless execution from both Airbus and engine manufacturer Rolls-Royce, along with consistent corporate yields across transpacific corridors. The first A350-1000s are set to enter service in early 2027, and at that point, maintenance metrics, cabin reliability, and connection volumes at ICN will be what determines if Delta's interim flagship can successfully carry its Asian ambitions alone, or whether it desperately needs some assistance.

text:
Walmart (NASDAQ: WMT) is offering a bundled subscription deal that could knock Amazon's (NASDAQ: AMZN) Prime membership off its pedestal. Earlier this week, the company announced a combined Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus membership for just $120 per year. That's $100 less than the two programs priced separately, and $19 less than Amazon Prime's $139 cost.

The bundle includes free delivery, 2% Sam's Cash on select purchases, $0.10 off per gallon of gas, and a choice between Peacock and Paramount+ streaming, among other perks. The catch is that it is only available as an annual subscription, and there's no free trial or monthly option available at this time.

Memberships have proven to be lucrative revenue channels for companies like Walmart and Amazon. Shoppers tend to spend significantly more with the merchant when they have a membership, roughly four times as much as non-members in Walmart's case.

So can Walmart's new subscription bundle dethrone Amazon Prime? Probably not. Amazon Prime is so deeply entrenched at this point that the mix of streaming, fast shipping, and ubiquity among consumers is almost immovable. However, Walmart doesn't have to beat Amazon to succeed. This is what investors should focus on.

This particular offering strengthens Walmart's flywheel and advertising business. Walmart stock trades at a hefty premium, leaving little room for stumbles this holiday season. Some investors may want to wait for a better entry point. Still, overall, Walmart is an incredibly strong business that just created a new product that will help solidify and deepen customer engagement.

Shares of Walmart have risen nearly 6% year to date as of this writing. The stock is trading at roughly 40 times both forward and trailing earnings. The company's e-commerce segment continues to grow substantially, increasing 23% in the fiscal 2027 second quarter. Walmart's membership growth was also impressive at 17%.

Whether it overtakes Amazon or not, Walmart is a worthy investment.

name: Microsoft
title: Microsoft, McDonald's, Verizon, and Others Tell Crypto Platform Not to Tokenize Their Stocks
authors: Kyle Torpey, Ece Yildirim, Webb Wright
description:
Both crypto startups and more traditional financial institutions have spent the past year promoting tokenized stocks as the next major use case of blockchain technology.
Microsoft, Alphabet, McDonald’s, Goldman Sachs, and Wells Fargo are some of the latest companies to reject plans for tokenized versions of their shares, joining previous objections from Verizon and others.
Microsoft and Alphabet joined Goldman Sachs, Caterpillar, McDonald’s, Qualcomm, and Western Digital in a new batch of objections disclosed on the 19th, according to Fortune.
These latest reports followed nine earlier objections from CoreWeave, Verizon, Applied Optoelectronics, Broadcom, UnitedHealth Group, and others.
Reality Tokenized stocks have been promoted by everyone from BlackRock to Coinbase as the next big thing in crypto, as proponents say the technology can enable 24/7 trading, broader access to U.S. equities, and more.
text:
Both crypto startups and more traditional financial institutions have spent the past year promoting tokenized stocks as the next major use case of blockchain technology. But many publicly traded companies aren’t interested in the sales pitch. Microsoft, Alphabet, McDonald’s, Goldman Sachs, and Wells Fargo are some of the latest companies to reject plans for tokenized versions of their shares, joining previous objections from Verizon and others.

Last month, AMC Entertainment CEO Adam Aron also publicly clashed with Robinhood over the fintech firm’s decision to tokenize the theater chain’s stock without permission, calling the practice “contemptible, outrageous, disgusting, detestable, inexcusable, vile.”

Companies Exercise Their Objection Rights

According to Reuters, at least 22 companies have formally objected to stock tokenization plans by OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (the parent of the New York Stock Exchange). Microsoft and Alphabet joined Goldman Sachs, Caterpillar, McDonald’s, Qualcomm, and Western Digital in a new batch of objections disclosed on the 19th, according to Fortune. Later in the week, Reuters reported six additional objections, including Intuit and Wells Fargo. These latest reports followed nine earlier objections from CoreWeave, Verizon, Applied Optoelectronics, Broadcom, UnitedHealth Group, and others.

OKXICE, which is co-chaired by former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo, announced plans this month to offer round-the-clock trading in tokenized versions of 63 U.S.-listed stocks under a temporary exemption from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). Cuomo downplayed the objections in a written statement to Fortune. “We always anticipated that, because this is such a dramatic and revolutionary change, many companies would want to wait and see how it goes rather than be the first to participate,” he said.

Applied Optoelectronics told Fortune it objected because the framework is new and its potential effects on pricing, liquidity, and volatility remain uncertain. “At this stage, we don’t see a clear benefit to AOI or our shareholders that justifies these uncertainties,” a spokesperson said. The company also worried investors might mistakenly believe it sponsored or endorsed the offering. Apple, Nvidia, and Amazon are among the companies that had not publicly objected as of the Fortune report, though notices sent in early October give them until early November to respond.

Tokenization Hype vs. Reality

Tokenized stocks have been promoted by everyone from BlackRock to Coinbase as the next big thing in crypto, as proponents say the technology can enable 24/7 trading, broader access to U.S. equities, and more. Of course, critics counter that a blockchain is not a technical requirement for those features and that much of the activity looks more like regulatory arbitrage by centralized entities seeking additional revenue than the so-called “democratization of finance.” Similar points have been raised about the industry’s heavy use of centrally-issued stablecoins and corporate-controlled blockchains, two common themes that are both found in Circle’s Arc network, which has an uncanny resemblance to the fictional Ecoin project from the TV series Mr. Robot.

For now, crypto platforms do not need proactive permission from the companies whose stocks they want to tokenize under the SEC’s Innovation Exemption, which was issued last month after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate. Instead, platforms must notify the company, which then has 30 days to object. Erin Martin, a partner at Morgan Lewis and former senior SEC lawyer, told Fortune, “If they don’t object within that 30-day notice period, the [venue] can go ahead and start to tokenize and list those securities.”

Martin also noted practical issues with the notice process, such as the risk that notices sent to a company’s main executive office get buried before reaching the legal team. An unanswered notice allows the platform to proceed after the deadline. The SEC’s rules do not clearly address whether a company can reverse its decision after the window closes.

Additionally, an objection only blocks trading on that specific platform under the exemption. It does not prevent other firms from offering tokenized versions overseas or through different legal arrangements, as Robinhood has done. But those alternative approaches are not necessarily immune to legal scrutiny, as AMC already challenged Robinhood over its AMC-linked tokens as part of the aforementioned dispute.

The SEC’s exemption also provides a five-year window for Tokenized Securities Venues to trade certain tokenized National Market System stocks without registering as national securities exchanges, provided the tokens carry the same rights and privileges as the underlying shares, including dividends and voting rights.

text:
Key Takeaways

Amkor Technology shares rose 4.7% on Wednesday after a new $1.3 billion agreement to add capacity for NVIDIA in South Korea, which brings their multi-year agreements to $3 billion.

NVIDIA is prepaying for Amkor’s capacity, which shows that advanced packaging has become one of the bottlenecks in the AI buildout.

The prepayments help pay for an expansion that took most of Amkor’s operating cash flow in fiscal 2025: $900 million of capex against $1.1 billion of cash from operations.

Analysts already expect normalized EPS to rise 71% in 2026, and the third-quarter report after the close on Oct. 26 is the next test.

Amkor Technology (AMKR) shares rose 4.7% on Wednesday after the chip packager said it’s adding capacity in South Korea for NVIDIA (NVDA) under a new $1.3 billion agreement.

That brings Amkor’s multi-year agreements with NVIDIA in Arizona and South Korea to $3 billion, and NVIDIA is prepaying to lock in that capacity. The news landed at 7:30 a.m. ET, about an hour after NVIDIA announced new capacity agreements with its supply-chain partners.

“Our partnership with NVIDIA underscores the critical role advanced packaging plays in enabling next-generation AI platforms,” said Kevin Engel, Amkor’s president and CEO, in the company’s release.

When the world’s biggest AI chipmaker pays a supplier up front, it’s telling you that supplier’s capacity is scarce. Packaging has become one of the things holding back the AI buildout, and NVIDIA wants its place in line.

That matters for Amkor’s cash. Its operations have brought in about $1.1 billion a year since fiscal 2021, while capital spending climbed to $900 million in fiscal 2025…

…leaving roughly $200 million of free cash flow. With NVIDIA prepaying, Amkor doesn’t have to squeeze all of its new Korean and Arizona capacity out of that.

Arizona came first. In July, NVIDIA agreed to prepay $1.5 billion for Amkor’s expansion there. A month earlier, Amkor signed a 10-year U.S. packaging partnership with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (2330).

So the two most important companies in AI hardware now have long-term deals with Amkor. And in September, Amkor raised its planned Arizona campus investment to $12 billion, which makes every prepaid dollar count.

text:
ChatGPT Atlas, OpenAI's standalone AI-powered web browser, "lasted less than a year before being discontinued on August 9, with its most useful features absorbed into ChatGPT." That is one entry on a list TechCrunch's Lauren Forristal published on October 24 under the heading "AI Graveyard."

The framing is flat: "The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations."

OpenAI's own casualties dominate the top. Sora, the video app, "struggled with high operating costs and user-retention challenges and shut down in March 2026." The ChatGPT super-app redesign was rolled back in July after users found the new interface "confusing and cluttered." Operator was folded into ChatGPT. DALL-E's role was reduced as image generation moved inside the main product.

Then come the outside names. Relay, a five-year-old workflow automation startup, closed in August 2026: as "OpenAI, Google, and other larger platforms built similar automation directly into their own tools, five-year-old Relay struggled to hold on to a reason to exist as a stand-alone product." Notion Mail is scheduled to shut down on September 22 after users opted for separate AI agents to handle email. Huxe, built by former Google NotebookLM developers, closed in May 2026. Yupp, "a free playground that allowed users to compare responses from hundreds of AI models side by side," closed in March 2026.

Character.ai, which filed for bankruptcy in October, is on the list alongside Apple's $250 million Siri settlement over marketing claims, Microsoft's roughly year-long delay of Recall over privacy concerns, Humane's AI Pin shutdown in February 2025 (assets later going to HP for $116 million), and Rabbit's R1, still on sale but underperforming.

The piece closes on a framing number: per S&P Global Market Intelligence, roughly 42% of corporate AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned, citing "insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, scaling difficulties, or weak user demand."

Something to think about

This quote reflects the emerging business models that prioritize environmental sustainability as a key driver for competitive advantage.

A biogas digester is a system that breaks down organic waste through bacterial processes in an anaerobic environment to produce biogas, primarily consisting of methane and carbon dioxide. description:
Une opération stratégique pour le géant français de la beauté, dont la famille Bettencourt Meyers demeure le premier actionnaire.
Derrière cette acquisition, c'est donc une nouvelle fois le groupe L'Oréal qui poursuit son expansion à l'international.
La famille Bettencourt Meyers, premier actionnaire de L'Oréal Une opération qui s'inscrit dans l'histoire d'un groupe intimement lié à la famille Bettencourt Meyers.
L'acquisition d'Innovist est réalisée directement par L'Oréal et non par la famille.
"Notre investissement dans cette start-up indienne innovante témoigne clairement de notre engagement indéfectible à étendre l'empreinte de L'Oréal en Inde", a-t-il déclaré.
text:
Une nouvelle opération qui vient renforcer l'empire familial. L'Oréal a annoncé, le 18 juin 2026, l'acquisition d'une participation majoritaire dans Innovist, l'un des groupes indiens de marques de soins de beauté en ligne les plus dynamiques. Une opération stratégique pour le géant français de la beauté, dont la famille Bettencourt Meyers demeure le premier actionnaire.

Derrière cette acquisition, c'est donc une nouvelle fois le groupe L'Oréal qui poursuit son expansion à l'international. Le numéro un mondial de la beauté entend notamment accélérer son développement en Inde, un marché particulièrement convoité par les grandes entreprises du secteur. "Cet investissement renforce l'engagement de L'Oréal envers l'Inde et accélère sa stratégie visant à se développer et à devenir leader sur l'un des marchés de la beauté connaissant la croissance la plus rapide au monde", explique le groupe dans son communiqué officiel.

La famille Bettencourt Meyers, premier actionnaire de L'Oréal

Une opération qui s'inscrit dans l'histoire d'un groupe intimement lié à la famille Bettencourt Meyers. Héritières de L'Oréal fondé par Eugène Schueller, Françoise Bettencourt Meyers et sa famille détenaient 34,79 % du capital du géant de la beauté au 31 décembre 2025. Leur participation, notamment portée par la holding familiale Téthys, en fait le premier actionnaire du groupe.

L'acquisition d'Innovist est réalisée directement par L'Oréal et non par la famille. Mais cette dernière reste au cœur de l'actionnariat du groupe qui vient de mettre la main sur cette nouvelle entreprise indienne. Une opération qui illustre la stratégie de développement menée par L'Oréal sur des marchés où les habitudes des consommateurs évoluent rapidement.

Fondée en 2019 par Rohit Chawla, Sifat Khurana et Vimal Bhola, Innovist s'est fait connaître avec des marques comme Bare Anatomy et Chemist at Play. Le groupe mise sur des produits de soins de la peau et des cheveux conçus à partir de recherches scientifiques et commercialisés essentiellement en ligne. Ses produits sont également disponibles sur les grandes plateformes de e-commerce, dans le "quick commerce" et auprès de distributeurs physiques.

L'Oréal acquiert une participation majoritaire dans Innovist en Inde

Le montant de cette acquisition n'a pas été communiqué. L'Oréal prendra toutefois le contrôle de la société tout en laissant ses trois fondateurs à sa tête. Ils conserveront une participation minoritaire et continueront de diriger Innovist avec les équipes de L'Oréal Inde. Le groupe français s'est également réservé le droit de racheter à terme leurs parts restantes.

Pour Nicolas Hieronimus, directeur général de L'Oréal, cette opération doit permettre de rapprocher l'expertise internationale du groupe de la connaissance du marché indien développée par Innovist. "Notre investissement dans cette start-up indienne innovante témoigne clairement de notre engagement indéfectible à étendre l'empreinte de L'Oréal en Inde", a-t-il déclaré.

Une nouvelle acquisition qui permet donc au groupe de poursuivre sa conquête du marché indien, avec la famille Bettencourt Meyers toujours solidement installée au premier rang de ses actionnaires.

name: L’Oréal
title: L'Oréal steps up quick commerce push in India as CeraVe expands into new cities
description:
Hieronimus said India was among the markets contributing to the improved momentum in SAPMENA, where L’Oréal reported 20% growth in the third quarter.
The company said it was outperforming the regional beauty market by approximately 1.6 to 1.7 times and gaining market share across countries and divisions.
CeraVe and La Roche-Posay expand their India presence L’Oréal is also expanding its dermatological skincare portfolio in India, with CeraVe growing from a relatively small base and entering new cities.
“India is one of the countries where CeraVe is still a baby brand, but growing fast and expanding to new cities,” Hieronimus said.
Hieronimus said L’Oréal remained confident about delivering a significant acceleration in full-year sales growth compared with the previous year.
text:
L’Oréal is seeing a turnaround in India, driven by improvements in its local teams, increased content creation and a stronger push into e-commerce, including quick commerce, as the French beauty major looks to accelerate growth across South Asia, Pacific, Middle East and North Africa (SAPMENA).

Speaking during L’Oréal’s third-quarter 2026 earnings call, chief executive Nicolas Hieronimus said India was performing well and that the company was investing more in creating content specifically for the market while accelerating its commerce strategy.

“We create for India much more than we did before,” Hieronimus said, adding that the company was accelerating in commerce, with a focus on quick commerce, which he described as an important part of India’s e-commerce market.

The comments come as L’Oréal sharpens its focus on local market execution and digital platforms to drive growth across a region that delivered a strong performance in the September quarter.

Hieronimus said India was among the markets contributing to the improved momentum in SAPMENA, where L’Oréal reported 20% growth in the third quarter. The company said it was outperforming the regional beauty market by approximately 1.6 to 1.7 times and gaining market share across countries and divisions.

The CEO attributed the region’s performance to a combination of favourable market conditions, improved execution and investments in digital capabilities.

CeraVe and La Roche-Posay expand their India presence

L’Oréal is also expanding its dermatological skincare portfolio in India, with CeraVe growing from a relatively small base and entering new cities. The company has also launched La Roche-Posay in the country, positioning the two brands at different price points.

“India is one of the countries where CeraVe is still a baby brand, but growing fast and expanding to new cities,” Hieronimus said.

He added that La Roche-Posay, which is positioned at a higher price point, had also been launched in India, with the two brands working together as part of the company’s broader skincare strategy.

The expansion comes as dermatological beauty emerges as a significant growth driver for L’Oréal globally. Hieronimus said the dermatological beauty market was growing at close to 10%, with the company’s Dermatological Beauty division growing at approximately 1.5 times the market in sell-out.

Its key brands, La Roche-Posay, CeraVe and SkinCeuticals, were all growing at double-digit rates, according to the company.

While CeraVe and La Roche-Posay are at different stages of development in India, their expansion reflects L’Oréal’s effort to build its presence across the skincare category through brands with distinct positioning.

Local content and digital commerce become growth levers

L’Oréal’s comments on India form part of a wider strategy to adapt its marketing and distribution to local consumer behaviour, particularly in markets where digital platforms are reshaping beauty discovery and purchasing.

Hieronimus pointed to Indonesia as an example of how the company had responded to competition from independent beauty brands on TikTok. L’Oréal restructured its content production to become more competitive on social platforms, helping it accelerate growth in the market.

He said artificial intelligence was increasingly helping the company produce multiple variations of content to meet the demands of different social networks and platforms, while improving the allocation of advertising spending across channels and formats.

The company uses its Beta IQ tool to support media allocation, with AI and data helping it improve the efficiency of marketing investments.

For India, Hieronimus highlighted the increased emphasis on locally created content and quick commerce, suggesting that the company is seeking to strengthen its connection with consumers while adapting to the country's evolving e-commerce landscape.

SAPMENA delivers 20% growth

L’Oréal’s stronger performance in India came as SAPMENA emerged as one of its biggest regional growth contributors in the third quarter. Hieronimus said the region’s beauty market was growing at a double-digit rate, while the company was gaining share across countries and divisions.

Vietnam continued to perform well, Thailand accelerated and Indonesia staged a turnaround, supported by improved digital execution. India also contributed to the region’s momentum.

L’Oréal said the Middle East market performed somewhat better than anticipated despite the crisis in the region.

Hieronimus said the company remained ambitious about sustaining SAPMENA’s momentum in the final quarter of the year.

L’Oréal reports 7.7% like-for-like growth in Q3

At the group level, L’Oréal reported adjusted like-for-like sales growth of 7.7% in the third quarter of 2026. Hieronimus said the global beauty market grew by approximately 5% during the period, with the company outperforming across most categories, divisions and regions.

Europe and SAPMENA were the company’s first- and second-largest contributors to growth during the quarter, respectively. Sales grew in all regions except Latin America.

The company expects the global beauty market to grow by around 5% in the fourth quarter and said it expects to outperform the market, although at a more moderate rate than in the third quarter.

Hieronimus said L’Oréal remained confident about delivering a significant acceleration in full-year sales growth compared with the previous year.

The company is also preparing to support its brands through the crucial year-end selling season, with investments in new product launches, advertising and consumer engagement.

For India, the combination of expanded skincare distribution, more locally relevant content and a stronger quick-commerce push points to a strategy focused on building brands and improving access as the beauty market evolves.

GTC 베를린은 사흘간 열리며, 멀지 않은 STATION-Berlin에서는 에이전틱 AI와 로보틱스, 피지컬 AI, 오픈 모델, 가속 컴퓨팅을 다루는 100개가 넘는 세션이 진행됩니다.
무대에 오른 젠슨 황 젠슨 황 CEO는 질문 하나로 말문을 열었습니다.
L’Oréal과 Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé, HSBC의 공통점은 무엇일까요?
에이전트에 지식 계층을 더하는 NVIDIA 이어 젠슨 황 CEO는 NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation을 소개했습니다.
유럽은 AI 경제를 짓고 있고, AI 팩토리는 에이전트를 돌리는 방향으로 진화하고 있으며, 피지컬 AI가 다음 프런티어라는 것이었죠.
text:
1980년 베를린 장벽 인근의 천막에서 출발한 Tempodrom은 여러 차례 자리를 옮긴 끝에 2001년 안할터 반호프 근처에 정착했습니다. 이후 이 상설 공연장은 콘서트와 갈라, 정치 행사를 품어 왔죠.

오늘 이곳에서는 전혀 다른 종류의 무대가 펼쳐집니다.

GTC 베를린은 사흘간 열리며, 멀지 않은 STATION-Berlin에서는 에이전틱 AI와 로보틱스, 피지컬 AI, 오픈 모델, 가속 컴퓨팅을 다루는 100개가 넘는 세션이 진행됩니다. 이곳에는 기자와 애널리스트, 파트너가 메인 이벤트를 보기 위해 모였습니다. NVIDIA 창립자 겸 CEO 젠슨 황의 키노트죠.

무대에 오른 젠슨 황

젠슨 황 CEO는 질문 하나로 말문을 열었습니다. L’Oréal과 Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé, HSBC의 공통점은 무엇일까요? 모두 유럽 기업이고, 모두 NVIDIA와 AI를 함께하고 있다는 것이 그의 답이었습니다.

이번 키노트는 파리와 런던, 스톡홀름, 더블린을 도는 일주일간의 유럽 일정 끝에 열렸습니다. 그사이 NVIDIA는 유럽 기술 생태계에 100억 달러 가까이 투자하기로 하고 1만 2,000곳이 넘는 파트너와 협력해 왔죠. “컴퓨터 산업이 수십 년간 발전해 온 끝에, 우리는 이제 새로운 산업혁명의 초입에 서 있습니다”라고 젠슨 황 CEO는 말했습니다.

그는 AI를 5층 케이크에 빗대 설명했습니다. 에너지가 AI 팩토리를 이루는 첨단 컴퓨터를 돌리고, 그 위에서 작동하는 모델이 토큰과 디지털 지능을 만들어 내며, 그것이 다시 모든 애플리케이션에 녹아든다는 것이죠.

“AI 모델이 등장하기 한참 전에 인프라가 먼저 있어야 합니다”라며 그는 인터넷에 네트워킹이, 전기에 전력망이 먼저 필요했던 것과 마찬가지라고 짚었습니다.

“이 AI 경제의 일원이 되려면 AI를 소비하는 데 그쳐서는 안 됩니다. AI를 생산해야 합니다”라며 “우리는 그 모든 것을 이곳 유럽에서 할 수 있고, 사실 이미 시작했습니다”라고 젠슨 황 CEO는 말했습니다.

새로운 형태를 갖춘 AI 팩토리

젠슨 황 CEO는 하드웨어와 시스템 소프트웨어, CUDA-X 라이브러리, 모델을 아우르는 NVIDIA의 풀스택 AI 팩토리를 AI 인프라를 짓고 운영하는 포괄적인 플랫폼으로 소개했습니다.

“이것이 AI 팩토리를 만드는 데 필요한 기술의 폭을 보여 줍니다”라며 “오늘날 NVIDIA가 만드는 것이 바로 이것이고, 유럽이 AI 생태계와 AI 경제의 일원이 되도록 우리가 뒷받침할 수 있는 토대입니다”라고 그는 말했습니다.

그는 본격 양산에 들어간 Vera Rubin이 NVIDIA 컴퓨팅 플랫폼을 모델과 대규모 언어 모델 너머로 넓혀 AI 에이전트 전체를 처리하게 한다고 설명했습니다. 최신 랙 스케일 하드웨어 제품도 여럿 선보였고요.

이어 젠슨 황 CEO는 NVIDIA DSX POD를 발표했습니다. 파트너가 모듈형 컨테이너 안에 완성한 NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI 팩토리를 출하 전에 통합·검증해 내보내는 레퍼런스 디자인이죠. DSX POD를 쓰면 부지의 유틸리티만 준비되면 현장 배포 기간을 6개월에서 단 14일로 줄일 수 있습니다.

“세계 공급망의 완전한 변화입니다”라며 “사람들이 데이터센터를 설치하고 짓는 방식을 바꿀 것이고, 그 결과 속도가 올라가길 바랍니다”라고 그는 말했습니다.

NVIDIA DSX AI 팩토리 플랫폼은 냉각용 물 소비를 최대 100%까지 줄이면서도 같은 AI 산출물을 최대 30% 적은 전력으로 만들어 냅니다.

새로운 컴퓨팅 플랫폼이 된 에이전트 — 그리고 공학 문제가 된 안전

젠슨 황 CEO는 에이전트가 생각하고 추론하고 반복하며 도구를 쓴다고 설명했습니다. 쓸모가 커질수록 토큰 소비도 함께 늘어난다는 것이죠.

그는 에이전트를 다섯 가지 요소로 이뤄진 존재로 설명했습니다. 모델, 그 작업과 메모리를 조율하는 하네스, 하네스를 격리하는 샌드박스, 지식, 그리고 도구입니다. 이렇게 보면 에이전트는 질문에 답하는 모델 그 이상인데요. 지식을 끌어다 쓰고 도구를 통해 행동할 수 있죠.

“가장 중요한 것은 에이전트의 보안을 확실히 하는 일입니다”라고 그는 말했습니다. 자율 에이전트는 파일과 자원, 네트워크, 도구에 접근할 수 있는 만큼 권한은 최소로 두고 모니터링해야 한다는 뜻입니다.

NVIDIA의 답은 새로 선보인 안전한 AI 에이전트를 위한 NVIDIA OpenShell 레퍼런스 아키텍처입니다. 에이전트와 그것이 영향을 줄 수 있는 시스템 사이에 자리하는, 커널 수준 샌드박싱을 갖춘 오픈 소스 정책 제어 런타임 NVIDIA OpenShell을 토대로 삼은 풀스택 설계죠.

그만큼 권한과 정책 집행, 모니터링도 상황에 따라 유연하게 바뀌어야 합니다. “에이전트가 실행될 때마다 권한은 매번 달라집니다”라고 젠슨 황 CEO는 말했습니다.

전문성을 경쟁력으로 바꾸는 오픈 모델

젠슨 황 CEO는 NVIDIA의 오픈 모델을 각자의 필요에 맞춘 AI를 만드는 출발점으로 제시했습니다.

NVIDIA의 프런티어급 오픈 모델은 산업 전반에서 쓸 수 있습니다. 언어를 위한 Nemotron, 월드 파운데이션 모델을 위한 Cosmos, 휴머노이드 로보틱스를 위한 GR00T, 자율주행차를 위한 Alpamayo, 양자-고전 컴퓨팅을 위한 Ising, 그리고 물리 AI를 위한 Earth-2가 있죠.

“우리가 곧 프런티어입니다”라며 “그래서 이 모든 분야에서 여러분께 모든 모델을 제공하고, 지금도 계속 작업하고 있습니다. 10년째 해 왔고, 앞으로도 계속할 것입니다”라고 그는 말했습니다.

NVIDIA는 모델과 데이터, 그것을 재현할 스크립트까지 제공합니다. 덕분에 기업은 특정 용도에 맞춰 자사 데이터로 모델을 포스트트레이닝해, 독자 데이터를 그가 말한 ‘소버린 인텔리전스’로 바꿔 낼 수 있죠.

“Nemotron처럼 대단히 뛰어난 오픈 모델에서 출발해, 자사 데이터로 여러분의 용도에 맞게 포스트트레이닝하면 당연히 초지능에 이를 수 있습니다”라며 “대단히 합리적인 선택이고, 필요한 기술은 오늘 이미 다 있습니다”라고 젠슨 황 CEO는 말했습니다.

에이전트에 지식 계층을 더하는 NVIDIA

이어 젠슨 황 CEO는 NVIDIA Agent Knowledge Foundation을 소개했습니다. 문서 속 비정형 정보든 데이터베이스 속 정형 데이터든, 에이전트를 기업 데이터에 연결하는 모델과 라이브러리 모음이죠.

그는 문서를 파싱하고 질의를 임베딩하며 관련 정보를 재순위화하는 Nemotron 도구들과 함께, 정형 데이터로 예측을 수행하는 새로운 NVIDIA Kumo 모델을 강조했습니다.

“결국 이 에이전트를 슈퍼 에이전트로 만드는 것은 회사의 지식에 접근할 수 있게 해 주는 일입니다”라고 그는 말했습니다.

NVIDIA CUDA-X — 에이전트를 위한 가속 도구

젠슨 황 CEO는 NVIDIA CUDA-X를 과학과 공학, 연구, 창작 전반에서 쓰이는 가속 라이브러리 모음으로 소개했습니다.

NVIDIA 가속 컴퓨팅 플랫폼 위에서 1,100만 명이 넘는 개발자가 개발하고 있습니다.

그는 이들 라이브러리가 시뮬레이터와 솔버, 데이터 처리 엔진을 가속할 수 있다고 말했습니다. 에이전트가 쓸모 있는 일을 하기 위해 끌어다 쓸 법한 도구들이죠.

“CUDA-X 도구가 에이전트에게 일에 필요한 연장을 쥐여 줍니다”라고 그는 말했습니다.

실험실과 공장, 엔지니어링 현장으로 들어간 에이전트

영상에서는 NVIDIA Agent Toolkit이 회사의 지식과 모델, 도구를 하나로 모으는 모습을 산업별 사례 세 가지로 보여 줬습니다.

Lila Sciences에서는 에이전트가 B세포 림프종 치료 후보를 설계하도록 돕습니다. 가상 실험으로 자동화 실험실의 작업 방향을 잡아 주죠.

Siemens의 에를랑엔 공장에서는 에이전트가 신제품의 양산 준비를 돕습니다. 변경 사항이 실제 생산 라인에 닿기 전에 디지털 트윈에서 계획을 시험해 보는 식입니다.

Dassault Systèmes에서는 엔지니어링 에이전트가 차량 설계를 다듬습니다. 시뮬레이션으로 문제를 찾아내 설계를 개선하죠.

“그리고 [이 모든] 지식과 도구는 여러분의 것입니다”라며 “여러분의 전문성이고, 이제 이 모든 것을 할 수 있습니다”라고 젠슨 황 CEO는 영상이 끝난 뒤 말했습니다.

분산 AI 인프라가 되는 통신사

젠슨 황 CEO는 AI가 통신을 바꾸고 있다고 말했습니다. 주파수 효율을 높이고 기지국을 분산 AI 인프라로 바꿔 놓는다는 것이죠.

그는 10만 개 사이트와 약 100기가와트 규모의 분산 데이터센터를 언급하며, 8년 가까운 작업 끝에 NVIDIA가 Nokia와 함께 T-Mobile 네트워크에서 첫 상용 통화에 성공했다고 밝혔습니다.

“이제 CUDA가 전화를 겁니다”라며 “AI는 우리가 통신을 다루는 방식에 혁명을 일으킬 것입니다. 주파수 효율을 엄청나게 끌어올릴 겁니다”라고 그는 말했습니다.

치료실로 들어온 AI

헬스케어·생명과학 리더들이 NVIDIA 기술 위에서 신약 개발을 앞당기고 환자 진료의 폭을 넓히고 있습니다.

예를 들어 NVIDIA와 Siemens Healthineers는 AI 기반 방사선 치료를 개발하고 있습니다.

Nemotron 에이전트가 치료 계획을 조율하고, Isaac for Healthcare 플랫폼과 Omniverse 라이브러리가 장비와 환자 해부 구조의 디지털 트윈을 만들어 종양 조준을 시뮬레이션하죠. 여기에 IGX Thor를 갖춘 Holoscan이 실시간 영상과 센서 데이터를 이어 줘, 환자가 움직이는 동안에도 실시간으로 조사를 조정할 수 있게 합니다.

젠슨 황 CEO는 적응형 방사선 치료를 피지컬 AI 응용으로 설명했습니다. 치료 중에도 환자의 몸과 종양이 달라지는 만큼, 시스템이 그 변화를 좇으며 방사선 조준을 조정해야 한다는 것이죠.

“종양의 모양이 바뀝니다. 치료를 받는 동안 신체도 변합니다”라며 “이 적응형 방사선 치료 로봇은 변하는 환경을 인지하고 종양이 어디 있는지 파악해 완벽하게 분할한 뒤, 그에 맞춰 방사선을 조사해야 합니다”라고 그는 말했습니다.

앞으로의 길: NVIDIA 자동차 생태계에 합류하는 모빌리티 리더들

젠슨 황 CEO는 NVIDIA Hyperion 컴퓨팅 플랫폼이 더 많은 차량 플릿에 설계 단계부터 들어가고 있다고 말했습니다. 자율주행 소프트웨어가 로보택시를 차량 호출 서비스와 이어 준다는 설명이죠.

Lucid와 협력하는 Bolt를 비롯해 Mercedes-Benz와 Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles, Einride가 NVIDIA Hyperion 컴퓨팅 플랫폼 위에서 선별된 자율주행 활용 사례를 선보이며, 레벨 3·4 차량은 물론 미래 로보택시 플릿에 적용할 가능성을 보여 주고 있습니다.

여기에 더해 Volvo Cars는 안전한 자율주행을 위해 Hyperion과 NVIDIA Alpamayo Stack 소프트웨어를 도입합니다. NVIDIA는 개발자가 자율주행차를 대규모로 개발·검증·배포하도록 돕는 새로운 AI·안전 기술도 함께 선보였습니다.

Volkswagen의 밴과 JLR, Volvo, Mercedes-Benz의 차세대 차량이 Hyperion과 호환될 것이라고 젠슨 황 CEO는 발표하며 “Hyperion에 오신 것을 환영합니다”라고 말했습니다.

로보틱스 연구자를 위한 레퍼런스 휴머노이드

이어 젠슨 황 CEO는 Isaac GR00T 기반의 레퍼런스 휴머노이드 Agile ONE SN을 발표했습니다. 31자유도의 몸체를 갖췄고 내년 출시 예정이며, 연구자의 환경 구축 시간을 몇 주에서 며칠로 줄이도록 설계됐죠.

이 플랫폼은 모듈형입니다. 연구자는 전체 워크플로우를 그대로 쓸 수도, 필요한 구성 요소만 골라 쓸 수도 있습니다.

“아주 좋은 출발점입니다”라고 그는 말했습니다.

이 제품은 NVIDIA의 개방형 피지컬 AI 스택 위에 서 있습니다. 데이터 수집을 맡는 Isaac Capture, 로봇 지능을 담당하는 GR00T 모델, 시뮬레이션 기반 학습을 위한 Isaac Lab, 런타임인 Isaac OS, 그리고 NVIDIA의 공개 피지컬 AI 데이터셋이죠. Agility Robotics와 Figure, KUKA, NEURA Robotics를 비롯한 파트너들이 이미 같은 플랫폼 위에서 개발하고 있습니다.

새로운 기계를 만난 개인용 AI

젠슨 황 CEO는 지난주 출시된 RTX Spark 노트북 이야기로 키노트를 마무리했습니다. RTX 그래픽과 NVIDIA의 풀스택 AI 플랫폼을 얇고 고급스러운 Windows PC에 담아 가속 창작과 몰입형 게이밍, 강력한 로컬 AI를 제공하는 제품이죠.

그는 이 제품의 1페타플롭 성능과 128GB 메모리를 2016년 OpenAI에 전달했던 DGX-1과 견주며, 크기 차이를 마지막 한마디로 터뜨렸습니다.

“2016년에 저는 1페타플롭과 128GB를 OpenAI라는 작은 회사에 전달했습니다”라며 젠슨 황 CEO는 청중 앞에 작은 기기를 들어 보였습니다. “이것도 1페타플롭에 128GB입니다. 다른 점이라면, 이건 이렇게 한 손에 들 수 있는데 DGX-1은 두 사람이 들고 계단을 올라가야 했다는 점입니다.”

이어 그는 에이전트가 Hugging Face의 Microduck을 학습시키는 영상을 보여 줬습니다. 에이전트가 코스를 꾸리고 Isaac Sim에서 로봇을 시뮬레이션한 뒤 학습 작업을 클라우드로 보내고, 학습된 정책을 다시 RTX Spark로 가져와 평가한 다음 실제 로봇에 배포하는 과정이었죠.

네 마리의 Microduck이 무대 위 젠슨 황 CEO 옆에 자리를 잡고 신호에 맞춰 앉고 일어서고 낮잠까지 잤습니다. 그는 이들이 RTX Spark에서 만들어졌고 클라우드에서 학습했으며 시뮬레이션에서 기술을 익혔다고 설명했습니다.

“너희는 RTX Spark에서 만들어졌고, 클라우드의 수많은 NVIDIA 슈퍼컴퓨터에서 학습했으며, 바로 여기 RTX Spark와 디지털 트윈에서 기술을 익혔단다”라고 젠슨 황 CEO는 Microduck들에게 말했습니다.

마지막 총정리

Microduck들이 주위에 모인 가운데 젠슨 황 CEO는 키노트를 정리했습니다. 유럽은 AI 경제를 짓고 있고, AI 팩토리는 에이전트를 돌리는 방향으로 진화하고 있으며, 피지컬 AI가 다음 프런티어라는 것이었죠.

“이것이 전부입니다”라며 “누구나 에이전트를 만들 수 있습니다. 유럽의 모든 기업이 AI 기업이 될 것이고, 이곳 유럽에 번창하는 AI 경제가 들어설 것입니다”라고 그는 말했습니다.

마지막으로 젠슨 황 CEO는 깜짝 선물을 하나 더 준비했습니다. 키노트의 주제를 코믹하게 되짚는 유로비전풍 피날레 공연이었죠.

가사는 OpenShell의 가드레일에서 출발해 — “자격 증명은 없다. 접근은 기각” “BlueField 위의 Sentry는 결코 퇴근하지 않는다” — 피지컬 AI로 내달렸습니다. 로봇 학습을 두고는 “학자금 대출 없는 로봇들의 대학”이라고 노래했죠.

결정적인 한 방은 이것이었습니다. “fungible은 fun 없이는 쓸 수 없다.” 색소폰 솔로에 이어 “We are Europa” 후렴이 뜨겁게 이어졌습니다.

“함께 유럽의 AI 경제를 만들고 AI를 일하게 합시다”라며 젠슨 황 CEO는 강연을 마무리했습니다. “좋은 GTC 보내시기 바랍니다.”

Is Jensen Huang pushing Nvidia into an AI loop?

/8 min read

Share

Share

ADVERTISEMENT

In just six months of this year, company filings show the world’s most valued chip maker has multiplied its support for its own customers to $288 billion.

At peak euphoria, flirtations come easy.

On September 28th, at The Korea Society’s annual gala dinner in New York, the founder, president and CEO of chip maker Nvidia had the room laughing over his Korean escapade, when he mentioned how an overexcited employee of Samsung kissed him on the lips. “I’ve only been kissed in the mouth by a man in Korea,” said Jensen Huang, amid peals of laughter. He went on to describe how he had also downed somaek [a South Korean cocktail made with beer and distilled alcohol from rice].

ADVERTISEMENT

The fact that the anchor, too, referred to him as a 'rockstar', shows the excitement around Nvidia and Huang given that it’s the world’s most valued firm at $5.19 trillion, and unarguably the poster boy of the AI boom.

While the human kiss was accidental, Nvidia is having a serious fling with its customers.

The company’s quarterly filing for the second quarter ended July 2026 shows the company owns stakes in the businesses that buy its chips, renting back their capacity, guaranteeing rent and giving some clients longer time to pay back.

ADVERTISEMENT

None of the above is illegal or forbidden but it’s the growing proximity and the intensity that makes the numbers a bit unsettling.

Nvidia’s support for its customers grew about five-fold in just six months of this year, from roughly $55 billion at the start of the year to roughly $288 billion, according to Fortune India estimates, based on the disclosure in the filings. [The company did not respond to questions sent by Fortune India on the contours of the arrangement.]

The $288 billion comprises equity stakes worth $98.9 billion that Nvidia already holds in companies, of which $47.7 billion are in listed companies (including $5.0 billion locked up until December 2027), $47.9 billion in private companies and $3.3 billion in infrastructure financiers. Besides, the chip maker has committed to $25 billion of equity investments, $36 billion of computing time it has promised to rent from AI cloud companies over a six-year period. These firms buy Nvidia chips, build data centres and rent the computing power out; whatever they cannot rent to other customers, Nvidia has agreed to pay for. In addition, the chip maker has $20 billion worth of data centre leases it has signed to hand on to third parties. The biggest one is the $108.5 billion guarantees, comprising $105 billion for OpenAI's Ohio campus and $3.5 billion for other AI cloud partners. Interestingly, SB Energy, the renewable energy and AI data center infra platform backed by the SoftBank Group, OpenAI, Ares Management, and Nvidia, will build and manage the Ohio facility, through a 20-year lease to OpenAI.

On the OpenAI arrangement, Nvidia mentions in the filing: “In exchange for the guarantees, the site will exclusively Nvidia AI infrastructure, subject to limited exceptions.” The guarantees end “upon certain events, including OpenAI achieving a satisfactory credit rating.” Currently, Open AI does not have a credit rating and in October 2026, AIR Platforms, an AI-driven rating firm, rated OpenAI BB+ speculative grade (junk), citing negative EBITDA margins. Simply put, Nvidia is lending its customers its own credit standing until a customer earns one.

ADVERTISEMENT

Why is Nvidia doing this

The filing explains the rationale directly: AI clouds and model makers currently lack the ability to secure long-term infrastructures contracts and investment grade financing capacity to secure the AI infrastructure necessary to grow. It also means that lenders are unwilling to fund the customers yet on their own.

Interesting, in the 2026 annual report mentioned that Nvidia has been “asked for financing arrangements” and that “We have not entered into any financing arrangements.”

ADVERTISEMENT

Six months later, the July 2026 filing states: “Financing arrangements with certain investment-grade customers, including extended payment terms under large, multi-quarter agreements, will continue to affect the timing of our operating cash flows.” Receivables rose to $24.6 billion in the first half while operating cash flow was $74.4 billion, against net income of $118 billion.

While the filing states: “We estimated that one AI research and deployment company contributed a meaningful amount of our revenue by purchasing cloud services from our customers,” it doesn’t name the company though its description fits OpenAI, the same company behind the $105 billion guarantee.

What’s pertinent to note is that equity stakes Nvidia hold is also beefing up its income statement. Unrealised gains of $23.7 billion from equity securities were added in the first half of the current fiscal ending January 2027, and about 17% of pre-tax income, against $2.1 billion a year earlier.

During the quarter, Nvidia also began a new business model with select AI cloud partners. The filing states: “AI clouds procure our data centre infrastructure products, and we commit to cloud service agreements, which the AI clouds can unilaterally stop providing to us and sell to third-party customers at more advantageous rates.”

“If you look at the fundamentals, the demand for the neo clouds is off the charts…what is missing in the middle is the working capital to fuel that growth,” Huang told CNBC in an interview.

ADVERTISEMENT

The risk factors in filing spell out who carries the downside: “If AI clouds do not successfully sell committed capacity to third-party customers, we have agreed to purchase that capacity.” In other words, Nvidia carries the cost of weak demand.

The CoreWeave stress test

What makes Nvidia strategy tricky is the current travails of CoreWeave, which provides high-performance AI computing infrastructure. Nvidia is its shareholder, its only GPU supplier, its customer and the buyer of last resort for capacity it can’t sell.

ADVERTISEMENT

CoreWeave’s 2025 annual report says that “all of the GPUs used in our infrastructure today are NVIDIA GPUs.” Nvidia also appears among its customers, under a master services agreement dated April 2023. In September 2025, Nvidia placed an order with an initial value of $6.3 billion. CoreWeave's filings say Nvidia “is obligated to purchase the residual unsold capacity through April 13, 2032.” In January 2026, Nvidia bought another $2 billion of CoreWeave shares at $87.20 each, taking its holding to about 47 million shares, roughly 11% of the company.

ADVERTISEMENT

The month the market tested the valuation: CoreWeave shares fell 15.5% on October 14 to about $66, as yields on its unsecured bonds rose toward 15–16%. The company’s debt had already grown from $8 billion to $21.6 billion, and $50 billion debt as of mid-2026.

At $62 a share, Nvidia’s 11.50% stake in CoreWeave is roughly break-even on cost: its 47.2 million shares are worth about $2.93 billion, against roughly $2.97 billion paid. Early shares bought at about $40 or less show a gain of some $530 million. The 22.9 million bought in January at $87.20 are down about $580 million, or nearly 29%. The fall is sharper since June. Nvidia’s 13F filing shows 47.2 million shares on June 30, when CoreWeave traded near $99.60, putting the stake at about $4.7 billion. At $62, that is a write-down of close to $1.8 billion that will flow through the P&L, if the price holds through the quarter. It may appear a small change given Nvidia’s quarterly profit of $59.7 billion. But what is not visible now is the pain that could build up.

ADVERTISEMENT

If CoreWeave’s finds demand weakening, Nvidia is obligated to buy unsold capacity. Microsoft is the biggest customer, making up for 67% of CoreWeave's 2025 revenue. Microsoft’s share though has fallen with Meta, OpenAI and others signing newer large deals. While CoreWeave’s largest customer is now 36% of revenue (Q2 2027), if long contracts that come up for renewal don’t play out as expected, Nvidia’s backstop will get triggered. [Backstop is like a minimum revenue guarantee that entails Nvidia absorbing part of the shortfall if a customer’s cloud capacity is not fully rented out]

ADVERTISEMENT

The case for the underwriting

The strongest defence of Huang's strategy is the size of the business. In the first of the current fiscal, Nvidia clocked revenue of nearly $173 billion, operating income of $63.7 billion and net income of $118 billion.

Much of the exposure is also deferred and capped. The backstops are not due in the remainder of the current fiscal. The OpenAI guarantees phase in from fiscal 2029, and the filing says they “are limited to defined portions of lease and power payments and not the full cost of the site or all of the tenant's obligations.” OpenAI “has agreed to reimburse and indemnify us for certain losses,” though the filing adds that “we may not recover amounts promptly or in full.”

ADVERTISEMENT

Nvidia's revenue is also less concentrated than a year ago. Its largest direct customer was 16% of quarterly revenue, down from 23%. The extended payment terms, by the filing's own description, are for “investment-grade customers,” not start-ups. And Nvidia says it will apply discipline: it intends to “focus our data center infrastructure initiatives on exceptional sites and apply the same discipline to these initiatives as we do to our supply-chain management.”

ADVERTISEMENT

Nvidia knows that it cannot play the game alone and in August 2026 had an understanding with large capital providers to establish independent financing platform to garner over $500 billion of third-party capital over time to support the deployment of AI infrastructure. But there is no sign of such a pool of capital coming up. “These and other preliminary arrangements may not lead to definitive agreements,” Nvidia stated in its filings.

ADVERTISEMENT

Is Nvidia entering a forbidden circle?

Given the scale of its commitments, Nvidia now owns, backs, rents from and extends credit to its chip customers.

For instance, media reports mention that AWS is taking deliveries of $5 billion worth of Nvidia GB300 server racks at its U.S. facilities, with an additional $3 billion of hardware to be purchased each month in the foreseeable future. The issue is lack of grid connectivity has resulted in idle servers. The aggressive purchase has for the first time resulted in negative free cash flow for the company.

ADVERTISEMENT

With leverage funding the demand for chips across big tech and rising interest rates make the equation dicey. If AI demand slows, Nvidia could lose orders, mark down its stakes, buy unsold capacity, extend more time to pay and face guarantee calls, all in the same quarters.

For a stock that has surged 10x in the past five years to hit all-time highs, valuations are not exactly in bubble territory at 27 times trailing 12-month earnings. According to analyst estimates, Nvidia's revenue is set to compound 61% over FY26-FY29, with earnings outpacing at 65% over the same period. That’s enough to keep the momentum going, the hitch is that a lot of it is baked into future earnings.

ADVERTISEMENT

While the party lasts, Nvidia’s circle of influence on customers will continue to expand given that last fiscal it generated $97 billion. But of every $100 of free cash flow Nvidia generated, about $33 went into customers and partners, $43 went back to shareholders, and what was left was just $24. Not surprising that Morgan Stanley has a neutral credit rating on Nvidia, stating: “…exceptional growth turns balance-sheet strength into a strategic AI financing tool and introduces new risks,” adding that the tail “remains too early-stage, opaque, and sizable to step in.”

ADVERTISEMENT

The bigger risk Morgan Stanley sees for Nvidia is that’s total credit exposure will hit nearly $200 billion by the end of 2028, with $170 billion in guarantees and backstops that are off the balance sheet today but will hurt in the event of a downturn.

Investors are drawing parallels of such circular financing with the telecom bubble at the turn of the millennium when telcos financed the build-out with roughly $1 trillion debt for laying fibre cables, equipment, M&As. When the 2000 dotcom bubble burst, reports indicate 80 million miles of fibre was ready but unused. The subsequent Nasdaq meltdown coincided with the implosion of WorldCom.

ADVERTISEMENT

Investors are questioning whether such dependencies could pose risks if AI demand or monetisation falls short of high investor expectations.

At the gala dinner, Huang did mention that “nobody suffers better than I can,” in the context of Nvidia’s near bankruptcy in the late ’90s. While the Nvidia of today is no longer the fragile start-up of yesteryear, history does rhyme. At some point, the AI trance music will stop, and Nvidia's filings show why the fling could prove costly.

title: Nvidia open-sources Flora to make robot video labeling 125x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra
description:
Up to 125x cheaper by Nvidia's own estimates In a test with 50 videos, Flora scored slightly better than GPT-6 Astra according to Nvidia, even though OpenAI's model was allowed to use its full reasoning capacity.
Labeling one hour of video runs about 72 cents with Flora by Nvidia's estimate, compared to roughly $88.50 with GPT-6 Astra.
On Nvidia's own DenseCaptionBench, Flora leads across all metrics for human recordings, but for robot videos the model comes in second behind Astra.
In a video with many short hand movements, Flora identifies 34 of 37 individual actions, while Astra catches only four.
The company has also been working for some time to offset the shortage of robotics training data through simulation and automated data processing.
text:
According to the paper, Flora covers all three. Nvidia says the system is already running during training of its GR00T models, annotating up to 200,000 hours of video per day across 512 GB300 GPUs. The models are available on Hugging Face.

Flora consists of three fine-tuned Qwen3.5 models. A 9B model splits videos into action segments, and a 27B model describes them while factoring in what happened before and after each action. A second 27B model called Flora-Rewarder takes on three roles depending on the prompt. It rates an episode's success on a scale of 1 to 5, classifies each half-second step as normal, suboptimal, or failure, and assigns scores based on self-defined rubrics.

Up to 125x cheaper by Nvidia's own estimates

In a test with 50 videos, Flora scored slightly better than GPT-6 Astra according to Nvidia, even though OpenAI's model was allowed to use its full reasoning capacity. Labeling one hour of video runs about 72 cents with Flora by Nvidia's estimate, compared to roughly $88.50 with GPT-6 Astra. Claude Opus 5 scored much worse in the same test and still cost about $42 per hour.

The Flora cost figures are projections, though, not production measurements. Nvidia calculated them based on an assumed rental price of $10 per GPU per hour.

Flora finds actions better, but Astra often describes them more precisely

On the public WGO-Bench, Flora is best at detecting action boundaries but trails Astra in overall score and falls behind Gemini 3.8 Flash in pure description accuracy. According to the researchers, the gains come mainly from temporal localization.

On Nvidia's own DenseCaptionBench, Flora leads across all metrics for human recordings, but for robot videos the model comes in second behind Astra. There's a methodological catch the researchers acknowledge, too. GPT-6 Astra evaluates the descriptions while also being one of the models under test.

Almost no other model catches mid-episode errors

On RoboRewardBench, Flora's error rate is 27.8 percent lower than Astra's. The paper attributes the gap to partially completed tasks. When a robot only tips a bottle over instead of knocking it off the table, Flora assigns 3 out of 5 points to match the human reference, while Astra gives just one.

Flora-Rewarder catches 53.3 percent of failed steps within an episode, while no competitor gets above 11.7 percent and Astra doesn't catch a single one. The tradeoff is that Flora falsely flags about 11 percent of normal steps as errors. Astra still leads on rubric-based scoring and trajectory ranking.

In a video with many short hand movements, Flora identifies 34 of 37 individual actions, while Astra catches only four. On the flip side, Flora sometimes splits longer actions into too many small steps and occasionally gets descriptions wrong. In one video, a robot hand wipes a plate with a cloth, but Flora describes it as folding a napkin.

Nvidia positions Flora as an open alternative to commercial services like Scale AI's Physical AI Data Engine. Researchers can use it to scale their own robotics datasets and test approaches like transferring human demonstrations to robots. Nvidia is investing billions in open AI models to keep developers in its hardware ecosystem and drive demand for its chips, and Flora serves that same goal.

The company has also been working for some time to offset the shortage of robotics training data through simulation and automated data processing. At GTC earlier this year, Nvidia showed a data pipeline that automatically prepares, multiplies, and scores training material. Flora adds detailed labels and reward signals from video to that pipeline.

title: 'Supercharging bras': The story behind Victoria's Secret's $6 billion turnaround - Business Insider
description:
There was a stretch of time in recent history when Victoria's Secret was deeply unloved by consumers and investors alike.
The bra business also remains Victoria's Secret's "#1 growth driver," the company said in its quarterly investor presentation.
Selman also played a role in revitalizing Victoria's Secret bra department, having learned "the bra part of the business" while running his own sportswear line.
UBS downgraded Victoria's Secret stock following its springtime surge.
Frazer, the decadeslong Victoria's Secret customer, says the appetite for VS Angel content is still roaring on her channel.
text:
There was a stretch of time in recent history when Victoria's Secret was deeply unloved by consumers and investors alike.

Scarlett Frazer, a 26-year-old fashion influencer who spends thousands at the store annually, is among the diehards who say they never gave up on VS amid its slog in the 2010s. But even she acknowledges the rough patch.

Caught in the cultural shifts of that decade that made the brand seem out of touch and its marketing in bad taste, and beset by competition, the business struggled.

Fast-forward to the present, and the baby pink stripes are back. Victoria's Secret, once known for selling lingerie with unabashed sex appeal, is in the midst of a major comeback, with sales roaring and its stock climbing to records after a yearslong downturn.

The turnaround can be chalked up to a series of strategic decisions that revived the company's status as one of America's supreme intimates retailers — as well as a broader nostalgia for the 90s that has jolted all sorts of brick-and-mortar retailers back to life, from Abercrombie & Fitch to Best Buy.

For Victoria's Secret, the key has been a reinvigorated brand that appeals to a younger crowd, as well as old fans sentimental for Victoria's Secret's 90s-era heyday, analysts told Business Insider.

Victoria's Secret is on track for its best-ever year as a stand-alone publicly traded company. The stock is up 69% year-to-date, marking its best yearly performance since the company was spun off from L Brands, now known as Bath & Body Works, in 2021.

The company's market cap is up $6 billion since October 2023, when its stock plunged to an all-time low of $13 a share.

The gains have been fueled by surging sales. Comparable sales, a measure that excludes distortions stemming from newly opened or closed stores, have risen steadily since 2025.

Prior to that, comparable sales had been falling consistently on a year-over-year basis, Mauricio Serna, an executive director at UBS, said.

Serna said Victoria's Secret's business inflection began as the company embarked on a new strategy laid out by CEO Hillary Super. He pointed to the firm's "victory lap" on bras in particular, with brassiere sales seeing mid-teens growth in the second quarter. The bra business also remains Victoria's Secret's "#1 growth driver," the company said in its quarterly investor presentation.

"This is a company that has struggled for several years now," Serna told Business Insider. "The turnaround is materializing."

The comeback is also partly psychological. Last weekend's Victoria's Secret Fashion Show drew a peak concurrent livestream audience of 3.64 million, up 33% from last year's levels, according to the livestream analytics firm Streams Charts.

"The brand has become sexy and fun and aspirational again, but in a way that feels relevant to today's consumer," Hannah Renger, an analyst who covers Victoria's Secret at Citrini Research, said.

Frazer said the retailer is re-entering mainstream popularity. She began to notice the shift herself in 2023, when she began uploading tutorials on how to create the iconic Victoria's Secret Angel look that went "insanely viral" on YouTube and TikTok.

"I honestly think Victoria's Secret is in a league of its own," she said.

'Supercharging bras'

For investors, the proof is in the stock price. Shares had mostly slid since its 2021 spinoff, but its fortunes began to reverse in late 2024, around the time Hillary Super, the former chief of Savage X Fenty, Rihanna's lingerie line, was brought in as CEO.

The upward trajectory for the stock started in the spring of 2025, when designer Adam Selman, another Savage X Fenty alum, was brought in as the firm's chief creative officer.

Serna said several issues plagued Victoria's Secret in the 2010s:

Limited product offerings. Prior to Super's appointment, Victoria's Secret rarely had new product launches, Serna said.

Heavy discounting. In the last decade, sweeping promotional deals appeared to be Victoria's Secret's main strategy for competing with other retailers, Serna said. The discounts ultimately hurt profit margins and drew lower-quality growth, he added.

Brand perception issues. Victoria's Secret became associated with an "exclusive" standard of beauty at a time when culture began to value inclusiveness. The brand was slower than others to adjust, Serna said.

The company also came under scrutiny for its treatment of women and its association with Les Wexner, the former CEO. Wexner, who enlisted Jeffrey Epstein as his personal financial advisor for decades, stepped down from his CEO role in 2020 and later left the board in 2021.

Super, whose role at Savage X Fenty included establishing a major partnership with Nordstrom, has made innovation one of her top priorities since taking the helm in 2024. Since she joined, VS has had a regular pipeline of new product releases, particularly in the bra department, an area management has said they're looking to dominate.

"One of the very first things that Hillary communicated was the opportunity to take what they call 'supercharging bras,' one of their core strategies for the turnaround and enhance the product offering on that front," Serna said.

Selman, the chief creative officer at VS&Co, has also played an integral role in the firm's reinvention. The fashion and costume designer, who made Rihanna's famous see-through "naked dress" in 2014, appears to have married the brand to a more innovative, fashion-forward aesthetic, Citrini's Renger said.

Selman also played a role in revitalizing Victoria's Secret bra department, having learned "the bra part of the business" while running his own sportswear line.

The strategy paid off. 2026 marked the first time the bra business has grown in the last four years, with bra sales accounting for around half of the company's sales growth last quarter, Super said in a call with investors.

"Hillary Super is a fantastic CEO, and one of the most important things that she's done is recognize what actually works for Victoria's Secret," Renger said, pointing to the brand's return to "aspirational sexiness."

Super has also played a critical role in refining Victoria's Secret's image and landing a more consistent marketing message, Serna said. At times, she's appeared to both lean into the brand's sex appeal — even changing the company's stock ticker from VSCO to VSXY this year — while widening the definition of sexy and shifting the company away from the supermodel aesthetic that dominated in the 90s.

The strategy has walked a fine line between reinvention and a return to the familiar.

Serna pointed to the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show, which was revived from a yearslong hiatus after Super started in 2024. This year's event, however, showcased both legacy Angels, such as Adriana Lima, as well as new influencers, lending to a more diverse lineup.

The annual feather-filled fashion show has drawn newer Gen Z shoppers as well as older people who may have been shopping at Victoria's Secret 30 years ago, Renger said.

End of the runway?

It's unclear how much further Victoria's Secret's turnaround has to run.

The recovery appears to be largely priced in from a valuation standpoint, Serna said. He also outlined potential risks, such as the possibility that the brand reverts to its aggressively promotional stance, or that other players begin competing more aggressively in the US bra market.

Other popular retailers from the 90s and 2000s that have made a comeback have stagnated recently as US shoppers feel the pinch of higher prices. Retail sales slowed in September, rising 0.8% for the month, per the Commerce Department. Gap, which made a high-profile comeback in recent years, is down 11% year-to-date.

"We think maybe there's not that much upside to the stock price at this point," Serna said, speculating that the company may see more subdued growth going forward. UBS downgraded Victoria's Secret stock following its springtime surge.

Others are hopeful the hype will endure. In a note, Bank of America said Victoria's Secret was likely experiencing a "Fashion show halo" that is expected to boost sales through the holidays.

Frazer, the decadeslong Victoria's Secret customer, says the appetite for VS Angel content is still roaring on her channel.

"It's an entire aesthetic, lifestyle and almost a little club that girls want to be part of. You're not just buying a perfume or a pair of pajamas, you're buying into that whole world," she said.

Victoria's Secret executives declined an interview request from Business Insider.

text:
Global beauty major L’Oreal said it is witnessing a “great turnaround” in the India market, where growth has further accelerated driven by haircare and skincare. It is also sharpening its focus on the online channel including quick commerce. The French cosmetics major, which released its Q3 CY2026 earnings on Friday, said it has closed the acquisition of a majority stake in Innovist, a digital-first Indian personal care house of brands including Bare Anatomy and Chemist at Play. The company , which had announced this acquistion in June, said this will further support the acceleration of L’Oréal’s business in India.

The beauty major said that its consumer products division in India witnessed double-digit growth in the September quarter. At the same time, “emerging markets delivered spectacular growth, particularly in Brazil, India and the GCC,” for the professional products division, it said in an earnings statement.

Speaking at the earnings call, Nicolas Hieronimus, CEO of L’Oréal said, “ India, where I was just a couple of weeks ago, is doing great turnaround there, both in terms of teams’ quality. We create for India much more than we did before. We are accelerating in commerce, with a focus on quick commerce, which is an important part of the e-commerce market there.”

In the skin care space, the company has also been focusing on strengthening the presence of dermatological beauty brand, CeraVe besides La Roche-Posay. “India is one of the countries where CeraVe is still a baby brand, but growing fast and expanding to new cities. We’ve launched La Roche-Posay also in India, a bit more expensive, but the two working together is good,” Hieronimus added.

name: Nvidia
title: NVIDIA, Competitors Vie for Robotics Developer Dominance
description:
The company that created these robots is not NVIDIA but Falling Robotics, a subsidiary of AI platform company Hugging Face.
The frontrunner is NVIDIA, which has already integrated its technologies into multiple stages of robot development.
◇Intel, AMD, Qualcomm Also Aim to 'Capture Developers First' Competitors like Intel are rushing to secure developers before NVIDIA’s ecosystem dominance solidifies in the robotics market.
On the evening of October 22, Intel held an event for robotics developers in Mountain View, California.
AMD is also promoting its ‘Ryzen AI Embedded’ processors and robotics development platforms.
text:
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang took the stage at the company’s developer event ‘GTC’ in Berlin, Germany, on October 21 (local time). Suddenly, four small duck-shaped robots appeared from somewhere. The robots understood Huang’s commands and moved accordingly. When he said, “Take a nap,” they immediately lay down, and when he said, “Wake up,” they stood back up.

Huang then revealed his intention behind bringing the robots to the stage. Pointing to NVIDIA’s compact AI computer, the ‘RTX Spark,’ he asked, “Weren’t you created here? Isn’t it amazing?” The robots were explained to have been trained on NVIDIA’s cloud supercomputer and learned to move in a virtual environment within the computer. The encounter between Huang and the robot ducks became a major topic on social media, and sales of the robots surged.

The company that created these robots is not NVIDIA but Falling Robotics, a subsidiary of AI platform company Hugging Face. However, NVIDIA brought them to the event because its technology was used to train and operate the robots. Tools such as ‘Isaac Sim’ for simulating robots and their environments in virtual spaces, ‘Isaac Lab’ for training robotic movements, and ‘Newton’ for calculating motion and balance based on physical laws were utilized. Even without manufacturing the final robot, NVIDIA demonstrated its strategy to supply the computers and software needed to teach and test robots, positioning itself at the center of the robotics industry.

As robots expand beyond factories and logistics centers into everyday life, competition over the semiconductors and software that drive them is intensifying. With the growing trend of mass robot adoption in industrial settings, securing technologies for development and operation has become critical. NVIDIA, leading the AI semiconductor market, is expanding its influence in robotics by supplying everything from chips to learning and simulation tools. Meanwhile, competitors like Intel are also vying to secure robotics companies and developers.

◇Will AI Ecosystem Dominance Be Replicated in Robotics?

Robots require computers and semiconductors to perceive their surroundings, make judgments, and move their bodies, along with the software to operate them. Therefore, competition in semiconductor-based advanced technologies is not solely determined by chip performance. It also depends on how easily developers can implement desired functions using those chips.

Once manufacturers develop robots using a specific company’s chips and software, switching chips later requires modifying programs and revalidating the robot’s functionality. Hence, securing developers from the early stages of the robotics market is crucial.

Semiconductor companies are supplying various software development tools alongside their chips. The frontrunner is NVIDIA, which has already integrated its technologies into multiple stages of robot development. These include ‘Isaac Sim’ for testing robots in virtual spaces, ‘Isaac Lab’ for training robotic behaviors, and ‘Jetson’ computers for executing AI on actual robots.

NVIDIA provides the technologies needed to develop, test, and operate robots in real-world settings. Previously, in the AI semiconductor market, NVIDIA established dominance by making its GPU software platform, ‘CUDA,’ a de facto industry standard.

◇Intel, AMD, Qualcomm Also Aim to 'Capture Developers First'

Competitors like Intel are rushing to secure developers before NVIDIA’s ecosystem dominance solidifies in the robotics market. On the evening of October 22, Intel held an event for robotics developers in Mountain View, California.

About 50 attendees from robotics startups and universities sat at desks, directly using software that helps AI operate efficiently on robots equipped with Intel chips. The practical session involved virtual robot arms on screens inspecting blocks for defects and moving them to different containers. It was a briefing session where Intel introduced its software to developers and taught them how to use it.

An Intel employee on-site pointed to a graph displayed at the bottom of the screen, explaining, “By monitoring the usage rates of the central processing unit (CPU), built-in graphics processing unit (GPU), and neural processing unit (NPU), tasks can be performed more efficiently.”

Intel provides the ‘Robotics AI Suite,’ a bundle of development tools needed for robot perception, control, and AI execution. Included in this suite is ‘OpenVINO,’ software that helps AI models run efficiently on Intel’s CPUs, built-in GPUs, and NPUs. By reducing the burden of connecting and optimizing multiple programs, Intel aims to make its semiconductors an easier choice for robot manufacturers.

AMD is also promoting its ‘Ryzen AI Embedded’ processors and robotics development platforms. It has shared development cases and code linked to ‘ROS 2,’ a widely used software environment for robotics. The strategy goes beyond simply selling chips to supporting developers through the entire process of applying the technology to actual robots.

Qualcomm has released the ‘Dragonwing IQ10’ processor for robotics and a reference design based on it. The reference design is a hardware and software configuration that robot manufacturers can use as a starting point for product development. By reducing the burden of designing systems from scratch, Qualcomm encourages robot companies to adopt its technology.

description:
